title: Surge orchestration conductor and tenant telemetry bridge
author: Ravi Shah
release_notes: Introduce a cross-pool surge conductor, tenant isolation gate, and a compact utilization fingerprint exporter for improved predictive scaling and incident visibility.
description: Motivation: transient multi-tenant microbursts frequently cause noisy autoscaler churn and downstream p95 latency spikes. This PR introduces a lightweight Surge Orchestration Conductor that coordinates short-lived surge commitments across pools, plus a tenant telemetry bridge that exports compact utilization fingerprints for correlated analysis. The goal is to reduce reactive overprovisioning, improve tenant isolation during bursts, and provide richer signals for the autoscaler without increasing metric cardinality. Changes include: 1) a conductor control loop that accepts tentative surge offers, serializes commit windows, and emits lease intents to pool allocators; 2) a tenant isolation gate that computes a per-tenant isolation score and enforces soft caps when isolation threshold breached; 3) a utilization-fingerprint exporter that samples the per-tenant seqlen/throughput/burstiness vector every 10s and emits a compact hash+sketch to telemetry to enable correlating degradations with surge events; 4) back-pressure integration with the request router so surge commits can be denied fast when global headroom is low; 5) config knobs behind runtime feature flags for rollout and tuning. This PR includes unit tests for conductor decision logic, integration tests for coordinator+pool handshake using the test harness, and a small e2e canary that runs against a dedicated staging fleet. See linked Linear ENG-4281 for heuristics tuning and SRE runbook updates. Rollout plan: feature-flagged canary on 10% of production tenants for 72h, escalate if p95 latency falls or tenant error rates climb. Backout plan: flip feature flags off to revert conductor and gate; telemetry bridge is read-only and safe to keep on. Impact: expected to reduce autoscaler-triggered warm starts by ~12-25% in observed synthetic surges and reduce p95 by ~30-70ms in staging traces. notes: Rollout staged with feature flag surge.orchestrator.enabled and telemetry.util_fingerprint.enabled. Can be toggled independently. Monitor metrics: surge.coordinator.leases_granted, tenant.isolation.score, util.fingerprint.sketch_size, autoscaler.scaling_events. If autoscaler events spike after rollout, flip conductor off and gather conductor.trace snapshots.
